children: By Walden Siew
Good morning, CFOs. Welcome back from the U.S. Labor Day holiday.

In case you missed it, my colleagues Theo Francis and Ray A. Smith teamed up and reported on an interesting labor trend over the weekend, about how unemployment among younger workers is at one of the lowest levels in decades.

And on the flip side (which should be of interest to anyone funding a college education), young professionals with college degrees are having one of their worst times looking for jobs. Moreover, it's even harder for those with advanced degrees or in the fields of science and technology, Theo and Ray write. Check out the details in their story here.
It's more fodder for those debating the value of higher education, and whether a college degree is still worth it.

I've discussed this topic with finance professionals and my own colleagues, and a general consensus is that the value of a liberal arts education should be of greater value, as students build long-lasting human skills that AI and algorithms cannot replace.

?? Share your thoughts: Is higher education still worth it today? And if so, what are the majors or disciplines that will be the most valuable for finance professionals? Hit Reply to this email to join the conversation, and we may feature your response in a future newsletter.
What Else I'm Watching
Meanwhile, in other labor market news, layoffs continue here and abroad.
U.S. job cuts. Jaguar Land Rover is cutting 4,000 jobs as the automaker contends with President Trump's tariffs, a sales collapse in China and big investments in electric vehicles.
This follows news last week when Volkswagen's supervisory board approved a plan to double job losses at the automaker to 100,000 amid intensifying competition from Chinese automakers.
Chinese Company Draws Fire for Laying Off 100 Grads a Month After Hiring Them

Gas prices hit Labor Day record. The national average price for gasoline reached $4.15 on Monday, up from an average of $4.08 a week ago, according to the American Automobile Association. The previous Labor Day record was $3.82, set in 2012.

What Else Matters to CFOs
Smart-ring maker Oura's IPO filing listed a surprise underwriter: Robinhood Markets .
It is the first official underwriting gig for Robinhood, the retail brokerage of meme-stock fame that has in recent years expanded its business well beyond equity and options trading.

San Francisco-based Oura, best known for its fitness-tracking rings, filed to go public on Thursday, in an offering that is expected to value it at north of $11 billion. Founded in Finland in 2013, Oura is popular among health and longevity enthusiasts and has many fans on Wall Street.
